key_insight: Early three-dimensional vorticity evolution in transonic shock–boundary-layer interaction is dominated by viscous and compressibility effects, with vortex stretching becoming intermittently appreciable during shock-induced separation.
engineering_relevance: Understanding the onset of three-dimensional effects can inform aerodynamic assessment of natural laminar flow airfoils near drag divergence and shock-induced separation.
method: Run high-fidelity 3D simulations of the SHM1 airfoil in normal-shock, drag-divergence, and shock-induced-separation regimes.
Compare spanwise-averaged 3D pressure and skin friction with previously reported 2D simulations.
Track streamwise and wall-normal enstrophy and analyze the compressible enstrophy transport budget.
evidence_signal: Across three operating conditions, the simulations identify an initial interval of near-2D evolution followed by departures in surface responses and regime-dependent redistribution of enstrophy-budget contributions.
watch_item: The study covers short-time evolution on one airfoil at three operating conditions, so long-time behavior and broader generalization remain unestablished.
paper_title: Onset of three dimensionality in transonic shock boundary layer interaction over a natural laminar flow airfoil
